REASONING:
Step 1 – Project framing  
- Objective: improve quality of tourism infrastructure and services, condition of natural and cultural heritage sites, and increase sustainable tourism in the Arequipa‑Colca corridor.  
- Scope: four components (tourism attractions & services, road‑water‑sanitation‑health upgrades, transversal institutional strengthening, Project Implementation Unit). 33 individual interventions.  
- Delivery model: Borrower = Peru; Implementing Agency = Regional Government of Arequipa (GORE) through a newly created Project Implementation Unit (PIU). Technical oversight by MINCETUR; steering and consultative committees; inter‑institutional agreements with municipalities and stakeholders.  
- Timeline: Expected approval 09‑Jul‑2026; expected closing 30‑Jun‑2032.  
- Budget: Total cost US$97.8 million; World Bank financing US$77.2 million; counterpart funds US$20.6 million.  
- Key stakeholders: MINCETUR, MEF, Ministry of Culture, SERNANP, municipalities, private investors, local communities, women’s groups, NGOs.  
- External dependencies: climate‑related hazards (floods, landslides, earthquakes), private‑sector investment, procurement rules, timely signing of inter‑institutional agreements.

Step 2 – Category sweep (candidate risks with supporting text)

| # | Category | Candidate risk | Evidence (≤ 25 words) |
|---|----------|----------------|-----------------------|
| 1 | environmental | Climate‑related floods, landslides, earthquakes could damage roads, sites and halt tourism. | “Climate hazards also pose a challenge for tourism… floods and resulting mudslides weaken transportation infrastructure, road closures impede access to tourism destinations.” |
| 2 | organizational | GORE Arequipa’s PIU has no experience with World Bank‑financed projects; capacity‑building needed. | “It does not have experience implementing WB‑financed projects, so capacity building and close supervision will be required.” |
| 3 | financial | Delayed recruitment of Financial Management (FM) staff may impair fiduciary controls. | “Delayed recruitment of FM staff… FM staff shall be appointed within two months after effectiveness.” |
| 4 | financial | Potential inaccuracies in accounting and reporting due to limited experience. | “Potential inaccuracies in accounting and financial reporting… the national accounting system (SIAF) will be used, supplemented by annual independent audits.” |
| 5 | financial | Historical delays in budget allocation and execution rates in Peru. | “In Peru, initial project implementation phases often experience delays in budget allocation and low budget execution rates…” |
| 6 | financial | Disbursements blocked until three Inter‑institutional Agreements are signed. | “No withdrawals shall be made… unless the Bank has received at least three signed Interinstitutional Agreements…” |
| 7 | stakeholder | Fragmented institutional landscape hampers coordination of multi‑sector investments. | “Efficient budgeting and implementation… hindered by lack of coordination within a highly fragmented institutional landscape.” |
| 8 | stakeholder | Grievances may remain unresolved, affecting community acceptance. | “percentage of project‑related grievances addressed by the PIU” |
| 9 | political_regulatory | Recent years have seen increased political instability in Peru. | “…and increased political instability in recent years.” |
|10| schedule | Project conditions (PIU creation, key staff, committees) must be met for effectiveness. | “The PIU has been created and its Key Staff appointed in form and substance satisfactory to the Bank.” |
|11| technical | Roads may still be unsafe if safety specifications are inadequate (high local fatality rate). | “Designs will adopt specifications that enhance road safety, given Arequipa's higher road fatality rate than national average.” |
|12| environmental | Work in protected areas (e.g., Salinas & Aguada Blanca) risks non‑compliance without SERNANP coordination. | “Coordination with SERNANP … will be required for work in the Salinas and Aguada Blanca National Reserve.” |
|13| external | Private investors may hold back until infrastructure upgrades are visible. | “private sector is willing to invest once they see that infrastructure and tourism offerings are upgraded.” |
|14| external | Project relies on external technical assistance for disaster‑risk finance and public‑investment reforms. | “leverages ongoing TA on Disaster Risk Finance, which is developing innovative insurance programs for public assets in high‑risk areas.” |
|15| organizational | Long‑term road sustainability depends on effective maintenance arrangements. | “the project will ensure that, once roads are completed, maintenance arrangements are put in place to ensure sustainability of the investments.” |

Step 3 – Evidence filter  
All 15 candidates are directly supported by statements in the appraisal document; none are removed.

Step 4 – Assessment & mitigation  

| ID | Likelihood (1‑5) | Impact (1‑5) | Justification | Mitigation |
|----|------------------|--------------|---------------|------------|
| R01 | 4 | 5 | Climate events are frequent in the Andes and explicitly listed as major hazards. | Implement climate‑resilient designs (drainage, slope stabilization, flood‑proof structures); conduct hazard mapping; establish emergency response plans. |
| R02 | 3 | 4 | Lack of WB experience is acknowledged; capacity‑building is planned but execution risk remains. | Deploy intensive training through GFPP; retain experienced advisors; set clear TORs and onboarding schedule for PIU staff. |
| R03 | 3 | 3 | FM recruitment has a two‑month deadline; past projects show possible delays. | Prepare TORs early; start recruitment process before effectiveness; use interim FM specialists if needed. |
| R04 | 3 | 4 | Accounting errors are a known risk for new WB‑financed entities. | Use SIAF for all transactions; conduct annual independent audits; provide accounting workshops for PIU finance team. |
| R05 | 4 | 4 | Document cites chronic budget‑allocation delays in Peru. | Submit budget requests immediately after loan signing; set up joint monitoring with MEF; establish a cash‑flow tracking dashboard. |
| R06 | 3 | 4 | Disbursement conditional on three agreements; signing can be slow. | Prioritize agreement negotiations before effective date; assign a dedicated liaison to municipalities; track signing status weekly. |
| R07 | 4 | 3 | Fragmentation repeatedly highlighted as a barrier to coordinated action. | Strengthen steering and consultative committees; define clear decision‑making protocols; hold regular inter‑agency workshops. |
| R08 | 2 | 3 | Grievance mechanism is part of M&E but its effectiveness is not guaranteed. | Establish a transparent GRM, publicize contacts, train staff on resolution, monitor KPI for % grievances closed. |
| R09 | 2 | 3 | Political instability noted but not currently acute. | Secure high‑level commitments (steering committee); embed project mandates in legal agreements; maintain stakeholder communication. |
| R10 | 2 | 4 | Failure to meet conditions would suspend implementation. | Build a condition‑compliance tracker; allocate resources to satisfy each condition before the effectiveness date. |
| R11 | 3 | 4 | Road fatality rate above national average signals safety risk if designs are inadequate. | Incorporate guardrails, signage, pedestrian crossings; conduct independent road‑safety audits; train local road‑maintenance crews. |
| R12 | 2 | 3 | Protected‑area work requires SERNANP coordination; risk of non‑compliance. | Early joint planning with SERNANP; obtain all environmental permits; follow ESMP guidelines; monitor compliance. |
| R13 | 3 | 3 | Private‑sector interest is conditional on visible upgrades. | Develop a clear investment pipeline; showcase pilot sites; offer PPP frameworks and “Obras por Impuestos” incentives. |
| R14 | 2 | 2 | Dependence on external TA could affect timeline if assistance is delayed. | Transfer knowledge to PIU early; document TA processes; include fallback internal expertise. |
| R15 | 3 | 4 | Sustainability of roads hinges on maintenance; past projects show neglect. | Set up a dedicated O&M fund; train local authorities on maintenance; include maintenance contracts in procurement. |

Step 5 – Consolidation  
All 15 risks are distinct and directly evidenced; they are retained in the final register.
